units.source: Tables
Tables are a powerful feature for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, since editing them is generally easy.
To create a table, simply press the table button and select with the mouse the desired amount of columns and rows, as indicated in the adjacent figure.
Since v0.107.0, the same menu starts with an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert table…__TRILIUM_PH_1__ item, for a table larger than the grid or to type its size instead:
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and select __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert table…__TRILIUM_PH_2__. A small form opens at the cursor.

Enter the number of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Columns__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (up to 100) and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Rows__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (up to 1000). The table can have at most 5000 cells in total, for example 1000 rows of 5 columns.

Optionally, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Use headers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and enter the number of __TRILIUM_PH_2__Header columns__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Header rows__TRILIUM_PH_5__. A table cannot have more header columns or rows than it has columns or rows.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

To close the form without inserting a table, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or click outside it. From the keyboard, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_3__ moves between __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert table…__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and the grid while the menu is open.

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the table is inserted from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button of the formatting toolbar: its __TRILIUM_PH_3__Insert table__TRILIUM_PH_4__ tile lists common sizes, from 2 × 2 to 3 × 4 (rows × columns). Tap one to insert a table of that size; to make it larger, insert rows and columns afterwards.
Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_0__
When a table is selected, a special formatting toolbar will appear:

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the toolbar does not float over the table. Instead, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button after __TRILIUM_PH_3__Undo__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5__Redo__TRILIUM_PH_6__ in the formatting toolbar at the bottom of the screen to show the table's toolbar there.
Context menu__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Since v0.106.0, right-clicking anywhere inside a table opens a context menu with the most common table operations:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert row above__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert row below__TRILIUM_PH_3__ insert a blank row next to the row of the current cell. When the selection spans multiple rows, the same number of rows is inserted.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert column to the left__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert column to the right__TRILIUM_PH_3__ work the same way for columns.

Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Set as header__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Set header up to this row__TRILIUM_PH_3__, depending on the selection, turns rows into header rows, which always start at the top of the table:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Set as header__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows when the selection starts at the first row, and makes every selected row a header row.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Set header up to this row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows when the selection is in a single row below the first, and makes that row and every row above it header rows.
Neither shows when the selection spans several rows below the first.

A check mark shows that the rows are already header rows. Choosing the item again turns them, and every header row below them, back into regular rows. For example, in a table with five header rows, choosing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Set header up to this row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ on the third row leaves only the first two as header rows.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Merge cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ merges the selected cells into one. The selected cells must form a rectangle.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Split cell__TRILIUM_PH_1__ splits each selected cell in two, either __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vertically__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Horizontally__TRILIUM_PH_5__. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_7__, in the same submenu, turns each merged cell in the selection back into the single cells it covers, keeping its content in the top-left one; cells that are not merged stay as they are.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Distribute columns evenly__TRILIUM_PH_1__ splits the combined width of the columns the selection touches equally between them. The other columns and the width of the table stay as they are. It needs a selection spanning at least two columns; a merged cell counts for every column it covers.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Cut__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Copy as Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_5__ act on the selected cells. Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_9__ open submenus with their variants, such as __TRILIUM_PH_10__Copy as Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_11__ and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Paste as plain text__TRILIUM_PH_13__; clicking __TRILIUM_PH_14__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_15__ or __TRILIUM_PH_16__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_17__ itself still copies or pastes:

Cutting or copying produces a smaller table holding just the selected cells. Pasting it over a cell selection replaces those cells; pasting elsewhere inserts it as a table of its own. Cutting clears the cells without removing rows or columns.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy as Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_1__ converts the selected cells to a Markdown table. A selected header row becomes the Markdown header; without one, an empty header row is emitted, since Markdown tables require one.

Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Paste rows above__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Paste rows below__TRILIUM_PH_3__, in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_5__ submenu, paste the clipboard as new rows next to the row of the current cell, instead of over the cells from the cursor on. They show only when the selection is in a single row, and, like __TRILIUM_PH_6__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_7__, only where the clipboard can be read:

A copied table becomes one new row for each of its rows, filled from the first column. When it has more columns than the table, the table gains columns, as with a regular paste. Other content goes in the first cell of a single new row.
The new rows are selected afterwards.
When merged cells join the row to others, the new rows go above or below that whole block of rows.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_1__, below the clipboard section, sorts the rows by the column of the current cell, in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ascending__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Descending__TRILIUM_PH_5__ order. See __TRILIUM_PH_6__Sorting rows__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Delete column__TRILIUM_PH_3__, below __TRILIUM_PH_4__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_5__, remove every row or column the selection touches, even when only some of their cells are selected.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete table__TRILIUM_PH_1__ removes the whole table and leaves an empty paragraph in its place. In a table nested inside another, only the inner table is removed.

Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Select__TRILIUM_PH_1__, below __TRILIUM_PH_2__Delete table__TRILIUM_PH_3__, selects the cells of every row (__TRILIUM_PH_4__Row__TRILIUM_PH_5__) or column (__TRILIUM_PH_6__Column__TRILIUM_PH_7__) the selection touches, or every cell of the table (__TRILIUM_PH_8__Table__TRILIUM_PH_9__). Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_10__ button, which selects the table as a whole, __TRILIUM_PH_11__Table__TRILIUM_PH_12__ selects its cells, so cell operations such as __TRILIUM_PH_13__Merge cells__TRILIUM_PH_14__ apply to all of them. In a table nested inside another, __TRILIUM_PH_15__Table__TRILIUM_PH_16__ selects only the cells of the inner table.
Right-clicking a cell that is not part of the current selection moves the cursor there first, so the menu always applies to the cell under the pointer.

In the browser, Trilium's menu replaces the browser's own context menu inside tables. To reach the browser's menu (for example for its spell checking suggestions), hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while right-clicking. The desktop application is unaffected, since its menu already includes the spelling suggestions. In the browser, the menu also offers __TRILIUM_PH_2__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_3__ only when the page can read the clipboard, which requires a secure (HTTPS) context and your permission; otherwise, paste with __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__V__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
Navigating a table__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Using the mouse:
Click on a cell to focus it.
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at the top or the bottom of a table to insert an empty paragraph near it.
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the top-left of the table to select it entirely (for easy copy-pasting or cutting) or drag and drop it to relocate the table.
Using the keyboard:
Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to easily navigate between cells.
It's also possible to use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to go to the next cell and Shift+Tab to go to the previous cell.
Unlike arrow keys, pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the end of the table (last row, last column) will create a new row automatically.
To select multiple cells, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while using the arrow keys.
Using touch:
Since v0.107.0, touching a table outlines the cell with the cursor, or the selected cells, and shows a handle at each corner of the outline.

To select multiple cells, drag one of the handles across the table. The cell at the opposite corner stays selected, so the selection grows or shrinks as the finger moves. The note and wide tables scroll when the handle reaches the edge of the screen.
Resizing cells__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Columns can be resized by hovering the mouse over the border of two adjacent cells and dragging it.

To give several columns the same width, select cells across them and choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__Distribute columns evenly__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button of the formatting toolbar or from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
By default, the row height is not adjustable using the mouse, but it can be configured from the cell settings (see below).
To adjust exactly the width (in pixels or percentages) of a cell, select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button.
Resizing with touch__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: Since v0.107.0, touching a table shows a bar at the bottom of the note, above the formatting toolbar on mobile. The bar has a segment for each column of the table, with a divider at the end of each column. Only the divider of the column with the cursor is a handle that resizes; the other dividers only mark where the columns meet, so a swipe across them scrolls instead. When several cells are selected, each column they cover has a handle.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To resize a column, place the cursor in one of its cells or tap its segment, then drag its handle. The table grows or shrinks with the column, and scrolls when the handle reaches the edge of the screen. The column snaps to its starting width and to the widths of the columns beside it.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To cancel a resize, drag the handle back to where it started, or touch the screen with a second finger.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To give a column and the next one the same width, double-tap the handle between them.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To select a column, tap its segment. To open the column menu, touch and hold the segment.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To scroll a wide table sideways, swipe along the bar.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: A wide table scrolls a little past its end, so the handle of its last column stays away from the edge of the screen, where a swipe navigates back.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: Wide tables__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Since v0.107.0, a table can be wider than the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content width__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Such a table scrolls sideways, while the rest of the note keeps its width.

A new table is as wide as the content. To make it wider, drag the right border of its last column past the edge of the content. The border snaps to the edge and holds there briefly, so the table is easy to bring back to the width of the content.
To set an exact width, enter a percentage above __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or a width in pixels in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__table properties__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
A table whose content needs more room than the note, such as a pasted table with many columns, also scrolls instead of stretching the note.
Wide tables scroll the same way in read-only notes and on shared pages.
When printing or exporting to PDF, a wide table is shrunk to fit the page.
Tables inside other blocks, such as block quotes, admonitions, collapsible blocks, columns or tabs, are limited to the width of their block and do not scroll.
Mobile support__TRILIUM_PH_0__

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a table keeps the width it has on a desktop and scrolls sideways, instead of squeezing its columns into the width of the screen. The full width of a table is the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Max content width__TRILIUM_PH_3__ set in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Options__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_7__ → __TRILIUM_PH_8__Content Width__TRILIUM_PH_9__ on the mobile device, 1200 pixels by default. For example, a table set to __TRILIUM_PH_10__ is 600 pixels wide.
To resize columns on mobile, use the bar described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizing with touch__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Long tables__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Since v0.107.0, the header rows of a table stay visible at the top of the note while you scroll through the rest of the table, and leave with the end of the table. This also works in read-only notes, on shared pages and in wide tables.

To turn rows into header rows, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Set as header__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__, or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Header row__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ button of the formatting toolbar.

To let header rows scroll away with the rest of the table, turn off __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Features__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Use sticky header rows for tables__TRILIUM_PH_7__. The setting applies to the current device only, and shared pages keep their sticky header rows.
Inserting new rows and new columns__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: To insert a new column, click on a desired location, then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button from the formatting toolbar and select __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert column left or right.__TRILIUM_PH_2__
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: To insert a new row, click on a desired location, then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and select __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert row above__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or __TRILIUM_PH_3__below__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: A quicker alternative to creating a new row while at the end of the table is to press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ key.
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: Both operations are also available in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which inserts as many rows or columns as the selection spans.
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: The menu of the block handle beside a cell, described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, also has __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert row above__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert row below__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: After an insertion, the caret moves into the new row and stays in its column, or into the new column and stays in its row.
units.context: Tables > Inserting new rows and new columns

units.source: Moving rows and columns__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Since v0.106.0, rows and columns can be reordered with the keyboard:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Up__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Down__TRILIUM_PH_7__ move the rows touched by the selection up or down.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Left__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Right__TRILIUM_PH_7__ move the columns touched by the selection left or right.
Merged cells are never split by a move. The rows or columns held together by a merged cell travel as one block, and moving toward such a block jumps over it entirely.
When the table has a header row, a header row moved below the header area becomes a regular row, and a regular row moved into the header area becomes a header row. Header columns behave the same way.

Outside of tables, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Left__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Right__TRILIUM_PH_7__ keep navigating the note history, and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_9__+__TRILIUM_PH_10__Up__TRILIUM_PH_11__ and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_13__+__TRILIUM_PH_14__Down__TRILIUM_PH_15__ keep moving the current paragraph.
Sorting rows__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Since v0.107.0, the rows of a table can be sorted by the values of one column:

To sort all the rows, place the cursor in any cell of the column to sort by, then select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ascending__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Descending__TRILIUM_PH_5__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_6__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_7__. The same items are in the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ button of the formatting toolbar.
To sort only some of the rows, select their cells in the column to sort by, then sort the same way. Sorting is not available while the selection spans more than one column.
Header rows always stay at the top of the table and are never sorted. A sort can be undone with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Z__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

units.source: Merged cells__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Rows joined by a merged cell are kept together and move as one block. The block is sorted by the value in its first row. When the block has more than one cell in the sorted column, the other cells do not affect the order, and a message says so: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Some rows were sorted together because merged cells tie them to each other__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
When the selection covers only part of such a block, the whole block is sorted.
Merging cells__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To merge two or more cells together, simply select them via drag & drop and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button from the formatting toolbar.
More options are available by pressing the arrow next to it:
Click on a single cell and select Merge cell up/down/right/left to merge with an adjacent cell.
Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Merge selected cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to merge the selected cells, the same as pressing the button itself.
Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Split cell vertically__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__horizontally__TRILIUM_PH_3__, to split a cell into multiple cells (can also be used to undo a merge).
Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to turn each merged cell in the selection back into the single cells it covers, keeping its content in the top-left one.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Merge selected cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_3__ are available since v0.107.0. Merging and splitting are also available by right-clicking the selected cells, via the __TRILIUM_PH_4__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_5__, where __TRILIUM_PH_6__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_7__ is in the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Split cell__TRILIUM_PH_9__ submenu.
Table properties__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The table properties can be accessed via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and allows for the following adjustments:
Border (not the border of the cells, but the outer rim of the table), which includes the style (single, double), color and width.
The background color, with none set by default.
The width and height of the table in percentage (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_0__) or pixels (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_1__).
The alignment of the table.
Left or right-aligned, case in which the text will flow next to it.
Centered, case in which text will avoid the table, regardless of the table width.
The table will immediately update to reflect the changes, but the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button must be pressed for the changes to persist.
Cell properties__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Similarly to table properties, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button opens a popup which adjusts the styling of one or more cells (based on the user's selection).
The following options can be adjusted:
The border style, color and width (same as table properties), but applying to the current cell only.
The background color, with none set by default.
The width and height of the cell in percentage (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_0__) or pixels (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_1__).
The padding (the distance of the text compared to the cell's borders).
The alignment of the text, both horizontally (left, centered, right, justified) and vertically (top, middle or bottom).
In a centered or right-aligned cell, each item of a bulleted, numbered or to-do list moves together with its bullet, number or checkbox.
The cell will immediately update to reflect the changes, but the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button must be pressed for the changes to persist.
Border and background colors__TRILIUM_PH_0__

The border and background colors of tables and cells adapt to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__theme__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the same way as __TRILIUM_PH_2__text colors__TRILIUM_PH_3__ do. A color picked from the palette, chosen with the color picker or typed in is shown in a lighter or darker shade that suits the current theme, so borders stay visible and text stays readable on the background. The hue stays the same, and the table keeps the color as it was picked.
Colors applied with older versions of Trilium are shown exactly as they were picked, until the note is next edited.
Older browsers that can't adapt colors show them exactly as they were picked.

Header cells are shaded to suit the current theme. To change their background in every table, set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ variable in a __TRILIUM_PH_1__custom theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or in __TRILIUM_PH_3__custom app-wide CSS__TRILIUM_PH_4__, for example __TRILIUM_PH_5__. A background picked for a cell still takes precedence.
Caption__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to insert a caption or a text description of the table, which is going to be displayed above the table.
Table borders__TRILIUM_PH_0__
By default, tables come with a gray border that is lighter or darker to suit the current __TRILIUM_PH_0__theme__TRILIUM_PH_1__, so it stays discreet on a dark background.

To change the default border of every table, set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ variable in a __TRILIUM_PH_1__custom theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or in __TRILIUM_PH_3__custom app-wide CSS__TRILIUM_PH_4__, for example __TRILIUM_PH_5__. Set it to __TRILIUM_PH_6__ to hide the borders of all the tables that don't have a border of their own.
To adjust the borders, follow these steps:
Select the table.
In the floating panel, select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Table properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
Look for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Border__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section at the top of the newly opened panel.
This will control the outer borders of the table.
Select a style for the border. Generally __TRILIUM_PH_0__Single__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the desirable option.
Select a color for the border.
Select a width for the border, expressed in pixels.
Select all the cells of the table and then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cell properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
This will control the inner borders of the table, at cell level.
Note that it's possible to change the borders individually by selecting one or more cells, case in which it will only change the borders that intersect these cells.
Repeat the same steps as from step (2).

units.source: Table indentation__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Since v0.104.1, tables can be indented as a block (the whole table moves, rather than just the content of a cell).
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__ button to select the entire table. Otherwise, the indentation applies only to the current cell's content.

Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to increase the indent, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to decrease it. Alternatively, use the indentation buttons in the formatting toolbar.
Markdown does not support indented tables, so the indentation is lost when converting to Markdown.
Markdown import/export__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Simple tables are exported in GitHub-flavored Markdown format (e.g. a series of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ items). If the table is found to be more complex (it contains HTML elements, has custom sizes or images), the table is converted to a HTML one instead.
Generally formatting loss should be minimal when exported to Markdown due to the fallback to HTML formatting.
